Toggle

A two-state button (aria-pressed): bold in a toolbar, mute, favorite. The variant is how "on" looks; "off" is always neutral, so the states differ by more than color. Has everything ray-button has and joins a ray-button-group.

Variants · off and on
offonon · teal subtle (default)FavoriteFavoriteFavorite outlineWrap linesWrap linesWrap lines lightMuteMuteMute filledLiveLiveLive raisedPowerPowerPower

Click any of them. Off is always neutral, so on differs by more than color. ray-button's default, transparent and gradient are not toggle variants.

Icon toggles

For toolbars where toggles share one value (bold / italic, alignment), see ray-toggle-group.

Sizes and states
xs sm md lg Disabled on Disabled off

Flip a toggle to see its change event.

File upload

A drop zone to pick files: drag, click, keyboard or paste. Checks type, size and count as files arrive, lists them as ray-attachment rows (thumbnails, remove) and submits them with its form.

Code

Open the code

In a raylang app

In a std/ui window with the native bridge, native makes browsing open the system's file dialog, with the accept types as its filter. The files it gives are paths on the user's disk, not bytes: they list like any other file (name, size, type) and the program reads them.

<form id="import">
  <ray-file-upload name="photos" native multiple accept="image/*" label="Photos"></ray-file-upload>
</form>
upload.addEventListener("change", () => {
  window.ray.send("import:" + JSON.stringify(upload.paths));   // ["/Users/ada/Pictures/a.jpg", …]
});

The form submits those paths under name. Dropped and pasted files are still File objects (upload.files holds both; a chosen one is a HostFile with a path). Without the bridge, or in a browser, native changes nothing.

<ray-file-upload> · RayFileUpload

A drag that can only be refused turns the zone red before the drop; refused files fire ray-reject and are explained under the zone. Without multiple a new file replaces the current one. Uploading is the app's: attachmentFor(file) gives the row whose progress/status/error to set.

Mode input

A text field with a menu of modes on one side: choosing a mode applies its attributes to the field (type, placeholder, inputmode, pattern…), so one control says what a value is and the value — a file path or text, an amount in € or $, a search by name or ID. Everything else is ray-input.

Alt+↓ opens the menu from the field.
Code

Open the code

<ray-mode-input> · RayModeInput

Declare the modes as <option> children (label, data-icon, data-hint, data-description, disabled, and data-set-<attribute> for each attribute the mode sets on the field) or with the options property. A mode's attributes replace the field's own while it is chosen and give them back after. The menu is a ray-menu of radio items in the field's shadow root; Alt+ArrowDown opens it from the field, and the trigger keeps the caret in the field.

PropertyAttributeTypeDefaultDescription

In a raylang app

Browse… shows only in a std/ui window with the native bridge. It opens the system's dialog for the mode, starting in the folder of the current path (save also suggests the current file name). // The program's side: ui.events() through bridge.handle, then the form arrives as usual.
for e in ui.events() {
    if (bridge.handle(e)) {
        continue;
    }
    if (e.kind == "message" && e.tag.starts_with("settings:")) {
        save_settings(e.tag.substring(9, e.tag.len()))?;
    }
}

    Document tabs

    The tabs of open documents (an editor's, a browser's): closable, with an unsaved mark, all over one shared panel; WAI-ARIA tabs with arrows, Home/End and Delete to close. The app closes them: ray-request-close asks.

    GETList releases POSTCreate release DELETEDelete asset

    Click a tab or use ←/→; × (or a middle click, or Delete on the focused tab) closes it. Closing the unsaved one asks first. The tabs share one panel, filled for the selected request.

    Code

    Open the code

    <ray-doc-tabs>

    Unlike ray-tabs, a tab has no panel of its own: they all control the element named by panel, whose content the app fills for the selected one. Closing is the app's: the ×, a middle click or Delete/Backspace fire ray-request-close, and the app removes the tab (after asking about unsaved changes, if it must). When the selected tab is removed, the one at its place is selected (change) and, if the closed tab had the focus, focused. More tabs than width: the bar scrolls sideways, fades the edge that hides tabs (data-overflow-start / data-overflow-end on the host), scrolls with a vertical wheel and keeps the selected tab in view.

    Command palette

    Search and run actions from the keyboard (Mantine's Spotlight): fuzzy search, groups, shortcuts, ⌘K / Ctrl+K; combobox + listbox pattern in a modal dialog.

    Open command palette

    On this site ⌘K belongs to the docs search in the header — another ray-command-palette, over the components and guides. This one has hotkey="" and opens with the button.

    Code

    Open the code

    In a raylang app

    With native-menus and the native bridge, the palette also lists the app's menu bar: every item, grouped by its menu, with its shortcut, the disabled ones greyed out. Running one gives the program the same "menu" event as choosing it in the menu bar, so the program handles it in one place.

    let n = bridge.system();
bridge.menu(n, "File", [ui.item("new", "New window", "cmd+n"), ui.item("open", "Open…", "cmd+o")])?;
for raw in ui.events() {
    let e = match (bridge.route(n, raw)) {
        Option.Some(e) => e,
        Option.None => continue,
    };
    if (e.kind == "menu" && e.tag == "new") {
        new_window()?;
    }
}
    <ray-command-palette native-menus></ray-command-palette>

    Declare the menus with bridge.menu (and change them with bridge.replace_menu and bridge.set_menu_item) so the palette knows them.

    In a raylang app

    With the native bridge, confirmDialog() asks with the system's modal dialog instead of a ray-dialog, with the same answer. A red confirmation (a destructive action) gets the warning style. native: false keeps the page's dialog, for a question that needs more than a sentence.

    if (await confirmDialog({ label: "Delete 3 builds?", message: "This cannot be undone.", confirmLabel: "Delete", color: "red" })) {
  window.ray.send("delete:" + ids.join(","));
}

    ray-dialog itself is always the page's: a form, a settings panel or a wizard stay in the page.

    Code

    Open the code

    In a raylang app

    With native and the native bridge, the menu opens as the system's context menu at the pointer: its items and dividers, disabled ones greyed out. The choice fires the same ray-select, so the same code handles both.

    <ray-menu native context>
  <div slot="trigger" class="file-row">report.csv</div>
  <ray-menu-item value="open">Open</ray-menu-item>
  <ray-menu-item value="reveal">Show in Finder</ray-menu-item>
  <ray-menu-divider></ray-menu-divider>
  <ray-menu-item value="delete" color="red">Delete</ray-menu-item>
</ray-menu>

    Checkbox and radio items show their check mark there too. Labels, nested menus, icons and colors are the page menu's only. A dismissed native menu fires nothing.

    The native menu reads its items the moment it opens, so items that depend on what was clicked go in ray-request-open, which comes first (a contextmenu listener of your own on the trigger may run after the menu's):

    menu.addEventListener("ray-request-open", (e) => {
  const row = e.detail.event.target.closest(".file-row");
  menu.replaceChildren(menu.querySelector("[slot=trigger]"), ...itemsFor(row));
});

    Blockquote

    A quotation set apart from the text (Mantine's Blockquote): a colored edge, a quote mark on it and the attribution below. A real <blockquote> inside, with the source's URL as its cite.

    Default
    The most dangerous phrase in the language is "We've always done it this way."
    Variants and colors
    Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability. The best way to predict the future is to invent it. The more I study, the more insatiable do I feel my genius for it to be. A closure stored in a variable cannot cross a fiber boundary in a native build.
    Spacing and edge
    Compact, for dense panels and sidebars. Roomy, for a quote that leads a section. Only the tint and the mark, no colored edge. The plainest one: a bordered box.
    A testimonial

    We moved our desktop tools to raylang and ray-elements in a week. The components looked right on day one, in light and dark, and the forms just worked.

    Katherine JohnsonEngineering lead, Orbit Labs
    Verified customer
    In an article

    Why the web components are form-associated

    Every field of ray-elements takes part in its <form> like a native control: it is submitted under its name, validated, reset and disabled by a fieldset.

    Form-associated custom elements enable web authors to define and create custom elements which participate in form submission.

    That is why a FormData built from a form full of ray-elements fields has every value in it, with no glue code.

    verbatim shows and copies the text untouched: a response body or a log keeps its indentation and its blank last line.

    Bring your own highlighter

    setHighlighter() hands every block to a library; its classes are painted with the ray-elements tokens, so the colors stay the same. Returning nothing falls back to the built-in one.

    <ray-code> · RayCode

    The code comes from the code property, a <script type="text/plain"> child (raw text: anything but a closing script tag), a <template> child (parsed as HTML: the easiest for markup, but a < that is not a tag, as in Promise<void>, breaks it), or the element's text; common indentation and blank edges are removed (not with verbatim).     <ray-icon> · RayIcon

    setIcons({ name: '<svg…>' }) replaces or adds icons (SVG markup or an SVGElement, drawn with currentColor); iconNames() lists them. An icon may have a filled version for a state (filled; "<name>:filled" in setIcons; iconNames({ filled: true }) lists them). The components draw roles ("ui.close", "ui.remove", "ui.expand"…; iconAliases()), each its glyph until the app registers the role: setIcons({ "ui.remove": … }) changes only the chips' ×. Sizes follow the font unless size; --ray-icon-size and --ray-icon-stroke tune the whole system.

    mirrormirror reflectsbooleanMirrored in a right-to-left context (dir="rtl"), for an icon that points along the text: back, forward, send, undo. The roles that do (ui.next, ui.previous, ui.first, ui.last, ui.disclosure, ui.separator) mirror by themselves.

    App shell

    The frame of an app (Mantine's AppShell): header, navbar, main, aside and footer on wide screens; on phones one column with a bottom bar. The main content scrolls, the bars stay.

    One app, three widths
    phone layout: app bar, content, bottom nav

    The app is a page of its own (open it) in an iframe: its drawers, menus and sheets open inside the device, and the shell picks its layout from the frame's width.

    Code

    Open the code

    In a raylang app

    In a std/ui window opened as full_content (the page under a transparent title bar, macOS), with the native bridge, the header becomes the title bar: at least as tall, with room for the window buttons, and dragging it moves the window (buttons in it stay buttons). With layout="alt" or without a header, the navbar and the main content start below the title bar.

    var o = ui.options(1100, 720);
o.kind = "full_content";
let h = ui.open_with("Builds", "ray://app/index.html", o)?;

    The bridge also keeps the window's background and title bar in the theme's background, so switching to dark, resizing or reopening never flashes the other theme.

    <ray-app-shell> · RayAppShell

    The layout follows the shell's own width (a phone-sized frame shows the phone layout). Below breakpoint the navbar and the aside take no room (a ray-sidebar there still opens as its drawer) and the bottom slot shows. It fills the window's height (100dvh) unless sized. In a std/ui full_content window (ray-elements/core/raylang.js) the header becomes the title bar: room for the window buttons, and it drags the window; with layout="alt" or no header, the navbar and main start below it.

    <ray-grid> · RayGrid

    The widths are the grid's own (container queries: xs 36em, sm 48em, md 62em, lg 75em, xl 88em), so a grid in a narrow column or a phone frame drops to fewer columns. It needs a width from its parent: in a flex row give it one or let it grow. A child spans with data-span="2"…"12" or "full".
